chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn Ahmad from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad from Zur'ah from Samaan, who said:

I asked him (peace be upon him) about two men who share a female slave, and they married her to a man. Then one of the men bought one of the two shares. He said: 'She becomes prohibited to him by his purchase of her, and that is because selling her is equivalent to divorcing her, unless he buys her from all of them (the co-owners).'

key_terms.بَيْعَهَا طَلاَقُهَا: Selling her is like divorcing her

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on marrying a shared female slave if one partner buys the other's share?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the specific mechanics of *tamlik* (granting ownership) for a shared female slave (*umm walad* or *sariyyah*), establishing that purchasing one's own share does not confer full marital exclusivity. It highlights the Shia juristic view that the sale of the slave's share is legally equivalent to a form of separation, requiring the acquisition of all co-owners' shares to remove the prohibition and allow full conjugal rights. This ruling underscores the precision in distinguishing between partial ownership and complete *milk al-yamin* necessary for marriage without a new contract.
